standard.title: Perform in informal and formal settings
standard.description: perform music in a range of forms they have learnt and/or composed in informal and/or formal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can perform from notation in informal settings, use rehearsal recordings and basic sound reinforcement, and plan/introduce performances (AC9AMU4P01). They have not yet performed in formal settings, presented via digital platforms, or engaged in systematic peer feedback cycles.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students perform music in a range of forms in informal and/or formal settings, using expressive elements, peer feedback and digital platforms to refine and present performances.

nodes.label: Expressive elements in rehearsal and performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can focus on specific expressive elements (e.g. dynamics and balance) during rehearsal and demonstrate them in performance to engage audiences and communicate ideas.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one expressive element to focus on in rehearsal; demonstrate that element in the subsequent performance.
nodes.typical_width: Rehearse and refine performances with a focus on expressive elements — dynamics, balance, tone colour, articulation (phrasing, staccato, legato); connect expressive choices to the mood and meaning of the music; focus on songs from cultural groups or in a language being learnt.
wider: Rehearse the same piece with different expressive interpretations — compare recordings and decide which interpretation best communicates the mood, with justification
Focus on tone colour and articulation across a cultural context the class is exploring — how do the expressive conventions of that style differ from what students typically apply?

response_modes.reason: Expressive performance requires the technical aspects to be automated enough that expressive intention can be maintained throughout. Rehearsal that explicitly separates technical accuracy work from expressive focus work — drilling technique first, then adding expression — builds this layered competence.

success_criteria: Can identify at least one expressive element targeted in rehearsal
Demonstrates that element in performance with a recognisable effect on the audience experience

nodes.label: Providing and responding to peer feedback
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can provide specific, music-based feedback on a peer's performance and use feedback received to make documented refinements.
nodes.minimum_width: Provide at least one specific music-based piece of feedback on a peer's performance; respond to at least one piece of feedback received by making a documented change.
nodes.typical_width: Provide and respond to feedback systematically — discussing how the composer indicates dynamics and how the performer/s interpret this; describing how tone colour and articulation communicate mood; making specific adjustments based on feedback and evaluating their effect.
wider: Conduct a structured peer feedback session using a specific framework (e.g. 'I noticed... I wondered... I suggest...') and track how feedback is used across three rehearsals
Compare feedback from a peer vs a recording vs the teacher — how does each source offer different perspectives on the performance?
nodes.hinge_reason: Peer feedback as a rehearsal tool — rather than post-performance commentary — is a new practice at Y5-6. Students who cannot give or use specific music-based feedback remain dependent on teacher evaluation for performance improvement. This skill underpins the self-directed rehearsal and evaluation practices required in Y7-8 and Y9-10.

response_modes.reason: Effective peer feedback requires a framework that keeps observations music-specific. Without structure, students give vague or personal feedback ('I liked it', 'it was too quiet'). Build a feedback protocol: 'Name a specific moment, describe what you heard using a music term, suggest one specific change.' Practise before applying in performance contexts.

success_criteria: Provides at least one music-specific piece of feedback on a peer's performance
Makes at least one documented change to their performance in response to feedback received

nodes.label: Performing in formal and digital contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present performances in formal settings and via digital platforms, adapting their approach to suit the context and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Perform in at least one context beyond the classroom (formal or digital); reflect on how the context changed the performance experience.
nodes.typical_width: Present performances via digital platforms (school intranet or website) including, if age-appropriate, interacting with audiences; stream or upload recordings; pose questions for online audiences; present performances in formal settings such as assemblies or community events; consider online safety protocols.
wider: Upload a performance recording with discussion questions for the audience — collect and evaluate responses, then reflect on how the online audience experience differed from in-person
Perform for an audience in a different year level or community group and adapt the introduction and performance approach for that specific audience

response_modes.reason: Performing in different contexts (classroom, assembly, online, community event) teaches students that performance decisions — pacing, introduction, engagement strategies — are context-dependent. Each new context adds to their repertoire of performance adaptations.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Digital performance contexts at Y5-6 introduce a genuinely new set of performance considerations (asynchronous audience, visual framing, online safety) that are increasingly relevant to real-world musical participation.
success_criteria: Performs in at least one context beyond the usual classroom setting
Can describe at least one way the context changed the performance decisions made
